sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-GFP immunocytochemistry on intact neurons; receptor function (e.g., dopamine-stimulated signalling) NOT MEASURED in the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: DRD5 is a class-A GPCR whose N-terminus (residues 1–40) is the sole extracellular terminus; the C-terminus (362–477) is intracellular. Anti-GFP immunocytochemistry on intact, non-permeabilised neurons can only detect an extracellular epitope, so the YFP must reside at the N-terminus. No signal peptide is annotated for DRD5, so the mature protein begins at Met-1 and a prepend (insert_after_residue = 0) places the tag before Met-1, fully extracellular and ≥3 residues from TM1 (which starts at residue 41). L2 independently confirms an extracellular tag at this same position. Full-length DRD5 tagged with YFP expressed in cultured hippocampal neurons (14–16 DIV); surface display of the tagged receptor confirmed by immunocytochemistry with anti-GFP antibodies on intact cells. The same paper (L2) further confirms an 'extracellular tag' on DRD5 by swapping SEP/myc at the same position. No residue number is stated in either clip.

sources.claim: The γ2-GABA A subunit and the D5R were respectively tagged with a superecliptic pHluorin (SEP) or a yellow fluorescent protein (YFP), expressed in cultured hippocampal neurons and characterized after 14–16 days in vitro (DIV) by immunocytochemistry, using antibodies directed against the GFP.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are from the same paper (PMC8125140) and describe the same N-terminal extracellular tag site on full-length DRD5; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip because it names the tag type (YFP) and explicitly reports surface display. L2 adds the myc-swap confirmation but introduces no new positional information. L3 (PMC11432204) describes a 'DRD5-nVenus' BiFC construct: by standard BiFC naming convention (receptor-tag), nVenus is fused to the C-terminus of DRD5, which is intracellular (residues 362–477); this is therefore recorded in other_positions rather than sites. Confidence is medium rather than high because neither L1 nor L2 states the junction residue explicitly — the N-terminal assignment is topology-derived, not validated at a named residue.

literature_other_positions.note: DRD5-nVenus BiFC fusion places the N-terminal Venus fragment at the DRD5 C-terminus (residue 477), which lies in the intracellular tail (residues 362–477); not a surface tag site.
